indicators.note: turning over flips the little word me so it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to bolster is to support or strengthen, as braces do

explanation.surface: Someone hugs their pillows, flipping over the bolsters on the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' makes EM from ME; 'bolsters' is a verb here, not the long pillows.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuddle someone is to hug or hold them close, a warm squeeze.

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
a model who posed for a portrait sat for it
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The Queen sat for a portrait with a final stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior replacement or imitation, a stand-in for the real thing.

explanation.surface: A patch of sky somehow found in an Indian city long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapsed star's region from which light cannot escape; also the cramped prison cell in Calcutta's Fort William where British captives died in 1756.

clue.text: Tiniest result of baling out over the Pacific?

definitions.text: Tiniest result of baling out over the Pacific?

parts.words: Tiniest result of baling out over the Pacific?
parts.note: a sailor scooping water from a boat and tipping it over the side adds a minuscule amount to that vast sea: an idiom for an insignificant contribution

explanation.surface: Someone bails water out of a leaking boat into the Pacific, achieving almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a contribution so small it makes no difference against the scale of the problem.

clue.text: Issue eastern chap with a note

parts.note: a chap is a man
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An eastern man with a note publishes something.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue as a verb means to flow out or come forth from a source.

clue.text: I am with a couple to do damage

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a couple is a pair, two of something

explanation.surface: Someone joins forces with a pair of others in order to wreck things.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it, lessening its strength or quality.

clue.text: Failure to understand Simenon, perhaps translated

indicators.note: translated means the letters are carried over into a different form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written (Georges Simenon, the Belgian crime writer), though the fodder needs one more I than is printed

explanation.surface: A reader misreads a Simenon novel, perhaps because it was translated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges the letters of SIMENON PERHAPS, but those give only fourteen: the answer needs a second I that the clue as printed lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A misapprehension is a mistaken belief or misunderstanding, a failure to grasp something correctly.

clue.text: Amateur and professional with new garment

parts.note: a pro is a professional

explanation.surface: An amateur and a professional are each given a new item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective piece of clothing tied over the front, worn by cooks.

explanation.surface: Someone is freed, then asks whether it will happen once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'Let out' again in its property sense: let out once more is RE- plus LEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means freed; split as re-leased it also means rented to a tenant a second time.

clue.text: Some science included Home Counties' plan

indicators.note: included means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Home Counties are those around London, in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
chem, short for chemistry, is one science

explanation.surface: A bit of science teaching was included in a regional plan for the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic arrangement or programme of action, a design for doing something.

indicators.note: holds means the phrase Latest arrangement contains the wanted run of letters

explanation.surface: The newest arrangement of a song features a percussionist.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer; the letters run across the end of 'Latest' and the start of 'arrangement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr played the drums for the Beatles, the best-known example of a rock drummer.

indicators.note: make-up of means the letters of Lancaster are made up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking about the inherited character of the house of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster suggests the royal house, which fits the hereditary theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral things are inherited or passed down from forebears through the generations.

parts.note: to take something is to accept it

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the fish's name is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Something happens to a person who accepts a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To take place is an idiom meaning to occur or come about.

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to spell the word for Father.
explanation.walkthrough: Father's short form PA is spelt P and A. A PANDA crossing was a type of British pedestrian crossing, a relative of the zebra crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelling out pa letter by letter gives P and A; the word is also a British signal-controlled pedestrian crossing of the 1960s.

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A black cat shows plenty of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounce means liveliness or energy, a springy zest.

parts.note: ea is an old dialect word for a river or stream of water
a rache is an old word for a hound that hunts by scent

explanation.surface: A hound suffers discomfort beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the dog beside the water. EA and RACHE are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is an ache inside the ear, a common form of pain.

parts.note: split in two, the name of this grid puzzle is an angry remark

explanation.surface: Someone says their fury is a mystery to them.
explanation.definitionFit: This puzzle is a grid of intersecting words, and a cross remark is an angry one.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the distress call surrounds the word for finest

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
best means finest

explanation.surface: A warning is issued about the finest fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Asbestos was a fireproof mineral fibre whose dust proved deadly, so the warning fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used as a building and insulating material.

indicators.note: about means the word for judges goes round the other piece

parts.note: to see something is to judge or assess it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone becomes furious about the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, boiling with rage.

explanation.surface: A remarkable bit of play at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or outstanding; in bridge, a signal is a card played to tell your partner something.

explanation.surface: A question about group learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a group of fish or of artists; it is also the place where children are taught.

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the other piece
bewildered means the letters of Senor are thrown into confusion

parts.note: OK means passable or acceptable

explanation.surface: A confused Spanish gentleman is asked about a game that is just about acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passable' looks like a judgement on the game, but it only supplies the two letters that go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue sport played on a large table with red and coloured balls.

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: A count of some 150 snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' points to the answer of that clue, meaning hugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold them tightly, to hug.

parts.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is time to think things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a verb, to ponder, but it is a noun: one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Alter the last word-middle letter of goodbye

parts.note: amen ends a prayer, so it is the last word

indicators.note: middle letter of means the central one of the seven letters of goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone changes the final word, the centre of a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to change or correct something, such as a text or law.

clue.text: Reasons the French sent back plant

parts.note: grounds are reasons or justifications

indicators.note: sent back means the French article is written backwards

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Reasons the French returned a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common weed of the daisy family with yellow flowers.

clue.text: These folk record vessel at Alton Towers

parts.note: them can mean these people
an EP is an extended-play record
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: These people record a boat at a famous amusement destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Alton Towers is a big British amusement resort in Staffordshire with rollercoasters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alton Towers is an example: a large amusement destination with rides built around a theme.

clue.text: Relics from the Pacific on show

indicators.note: from means the wanted letters are taken out of the phrase Pacific on show

explanation.surface: Artefacts from the South Seas are on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are religious images venerated as sacred objects, much like holy relics.

explanation.surface: Backing a railway loop.
explanation.definitionFit: Siding means taking someone's part; it is also a short track off the main railway line.

indicators.note: flying means the letters of send gear are sent scattering into a new order

explanation.surface: Grenades cause kit to be blown everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenades are small explosive devices thrown by hand.
